name: Emotional Hold Time
additional_sources: transcripts/what not to do in editing.txt
use_when: The scene asks the viewer to believe a feeling, realization, failure, or hesitation.
A face or reaction carries more meaning than the spoken line.
The first cut feels technically clean but emotionally thin.
A sensitive documentary moment needs empathy, grief, shock, or aftermath to register.
The viewer is already committed to a long-form piece and the scene needs observation more than speed.
A short-form human moment needs enough time to feel warm, imperfect, or connective before the story resumes.
avoid_when: The hold adds no new feeling, information, or tension.
The pacing target demands compression and the emotional beat is not central.
The held shot contains distracting mistakes, dead air, or irrelevant action.
The edit is short-form feed content where the emotional beat is not central and the user requested maximum compression.
The hold is only unshaped dead air rather than a readable human reaction.

timeline_pattern.pre_hold: Give the viewer time to connect to the face before the line or action.
timeline_pattern.post_hold: Hold after the line or action so the consequence can land.
timeline_pattern.ab_test: Create at least two timing versions when the emotional belief is uncertain.
timeline_pattern.sensitive_subject_hold: For grief, survivor guilt, danger, or destruction, test a 2-5 second reaction hold before cutting away.
timeline_pattern.short_form_human_hold: For fast-scroll human moments, hold only until the connection beat lands, then reset before momentum dies.

motion.rule: Avoid unnecessary motion during the hold.
motion.allowed: Very slow push-in if it increases attention without announcing itself.
motion.avoid: Fast zooms, wipes, or kinetic graphics during a moment whose power is stillness.

sound.rule: Keep natural pauses, breaths, and room tone smooth.
sound.mix: Music should support the feeling without pushing the viewer faster than the performance.
sound.quiet_rule: Silence or low room tone can be stronger than dialogue when the viewer needs to study the image.

captions.rule: Let captions disappear or settle during quiet reactions when text is no longer needed.
captions.avoid: Late caption animation over a silent emotional face.

color.rule: Maintain facial readability and emotional tone consistency across the hold.

implementation.ffmpeg: Test alternate holds by changing segment in/out points and rendering short review clips. Use waveforms to ensure room tone and breath transitions stay smooth.
implementation.remotion: Represent pre-hold and post-hold as frame counts that can be tuned independently.
implementation.blender: If adding camera movement, use subtle interpolation and avoid drawing attention away from the performance.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Extend the clip before or after the spoken moment; remove auto effects and keep the reaction visible.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use rolling edits and duplicate sequence versions to compare emotional timing.

common_mistakes: Trimming a major emotion until it becomes unbelievable.
Holding long without a readable change.
Cutting away from a sad or shaken subject before the viewer can feel the emotion.
Assuming long-form documentary always needs dialogue or a cut every few seconds.
Cutting a warm human interruption before the viewer can feel the connection.
Letting music, captions, or graphics rush the emotional beat.
qc: Does the viewer have time to feel the emotion before moving on?
Does the hold reveal a change rather than just add duration?
Does the scene still feel intentional when watched cold?
Are audio room tone and ambience smooth through the hold?
For sensitive scenes, did the edit allow the viewer to study the face, object, or destruction?
Was a slower version tested before choosing a fast cut?
In short-form, does the hold create connection without becoming dead air?
